title.narrative: Strengthened constituents capacity to integrate skills development into sectoral and national strategy to reduce skills mismatches and enhance access to the labour market

description.narrative: Trinidad and Tobago’s economy is actively engaged in diversifying the country’s economy. Improving productivity and building businesses highly competitive at the international level are among the objectives of Vision 2030, the country’s national development strategy. In support to increased productivity and competitiveness, Vision 2030 recognizes the need to align the education and training offer to the current and future labour market needs while keeping up with technological advancements. Moreover, it emphasizes a continuous renewal and upgrading of the skills of its workforce to accelerate competitiveness and technological advancement. The National Institute of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology (NIHERST) is leading the availability of information to guide policy development, updating training programs and provide career guidance to the actual and future workforce. In partnership with the ILO, NIHERST recently launched five publications on skills needs and STEM demand in five key sectors for the economic development of Trinidad and Tobago. In 2026-2027, the ILO continues to support NIHERST, by providing technical advice to disseminate research findings and coordinating with employers, workers, and education institutions to promote better alignment between education, training, and labour market demands in emerging sectors.
